title: Promote §§42–44 governed-decision persistence/replay candidate into architecture authority before decomposition
context: After Muse (§41), ChatGPT concrete reconciliation (§42), Codex falsifier (§43, NARROWED) and Kiro input-bundle trace (§44, SURVIVES), the candidate was judged complete enough for an architecture decision.
evidence_at_time: Kiro §40 gap audit at 53aab6b; Codex §43 at 4d43de8; Kiro §44 at d0f953a; existing OpportunityHistoryController append pattern; SQLite/DatabaseManager migrations.
alternatives: §45 records only 'A'; other options (B, …) are not recorded in this segment
principal_wording: A — promote the §§42–44 reconciled candidate into Wheelwright architecture authority before decomposition.
rationale: Recorded as preserved in §45 sections (strategic/AR/ADR reconciliation, simplicity check); no separate Principal rationale text.
expected_consequences: Architecture authority in 07-architecture-current.md and ADR-019; decomposition may proceed after roadmap-projection regeneration.
implementation: ADR-019 (docs/07c-adrs.md:690-771); 07-architecture-current.md:538-685; Doc 65 slice with migration 010_governed_decision.sql (ADR-019 impl note 2026-09-26).
subsequent: Realized slice exercised only Governed Context Version and Lifecycle Decision Record; Disposition role defined-but-unused; added subject_scope_association table.
notes: §45 says 'now ratified'; ADR-019 status 'Accepted'. Principal's literal input appears to be the option letter.

title: Java backend + existing SQLite is durable owner of three logical record roles (Governed Context Version, Lifecycle Decision Record, Operator Disposition Record), account-partitioned by opaque brokerageAccountId
context: §38/§40 left persistence ownership as the one unresolved boundary; Muse showed full server custody not logically required; §42 chose direct semantic persistence in SQLite as engineering minimum.
evidence_at_time: Existing SQLite + numbered migrations; browser→backend append precedent; browser-local account registry; single-operator deployment.
alternatives: client-only semantic history + opaque encrypted backup + cryptographic notary/anchor (rejected §42)
hash-only anchoring (rejected: would need a second durable payload store)
rationale: 'This is smaller in Wheelwright than Muse's opaque-blob + cryptographic-anchor model because Wheelwright already owns a durable semantic SQLite boundary.' (§42, 6344); 'engineering-minimality conclusion, not a claim that full server custody is logically necessary' (6115).
expected_consequences: Browser-local storage no longer architectural owner of governed-decision history (7085); backend timestamps/validates/appends, does not decide.
implementation: migration 010_governed_decision.sql: governed_context_version, governed_decision, subject_scope_association (ADR-019 impl note).
subsequent: Disposition table not realized in first slice.
notes: Tension with steering architecture.md:44 'backend must NOT … know about portfolio state' (S61D-E038).

title: Deterministic lifecycle DECIDE remains browser-side; persistence ownership ≠ computation placement
context: Separation first articulated §38 and preserved by Kiro §40 and Muse §41.
evidence_at_time: Current DECIDE pure/deterministic in browser; no invariant requires moving it.
rationale: 'No current invariant earns this move.' Would combine persistence work with recommendation-location migration.
expected_consequences: Moving DECIDE server-side remains a separate future architecture decision.

title: Lifecycle Decision Record contains canonical exact load-bearing input bundle incl. resolved policy/default/threshold values and evaluator version; ids/hashes are provenance, not recovery
context: Codex §43 falsified §42's 'evidence generation / provenance refs' as replay material; Kiro §44 extended to in-code policy literals.
evidence_at_time: Evidence payload rows overwritten in place; lifecycle policy is unversioned frozen code default (DEFAULT_LIFECYCLE_POLICY, DEFAULT_BTC_REVIEW_THRESHOLDS).
alternatives: immutable recoverable evidence payload referenced by the Decision (equivalent but larger; §43 6431-6436)
rationale: 'A hash can verify a recovered input bundle; it cannot recover an input bundle that was never durably retained.' (6452)
expected_consequences: Future evaluators consuming more inputs must replay-bind them; decomposition must define canonical serialization (sorted fields, null vs absent, UTC, enum spellings, recorded_at excluded from hash).
implementation: Executable replay re-runs pinned evaluator version against recovered bundle (ADR-019 impl note).
amendments: Narrows §42 field 'evidence_generation / exact evidence provenance refs' (6159).
notes: ADR-019 delegates canonicalization rules to decomposition; §44 canonicalization list not carried into ADR.

title: Bitemporal discipline: backend-assigned recorded_at distinct from effective/decided/acted time; replay from pinned context_version_id; as-of resolution applies recorded-time knowledge cutoff
context: Muse §41 bitemporal tightening; Codex §43 query invariant.
rationale: Backdated amendment must not masquerade as contemporaneously known governance.
expected_consequences: Later governance changes never enter an earlier Decision's knowledge set.
subsequent: ADR-019 bitemporal semantics cited later in 07c-adrs.md:865 and :912 (attestation / continuity evidence).
notes: §43's default knowledge cutoff = Decision's own recorded time (6474) not stated in ADR-019.

title: Allocation Purpose / Mandate stays upstream governance provenance; DECIDE input contract excludes purpose label
context: §35 model carried through §37 item 4, §39 PTS/Sawdust, Muse §41, §42 safeguard, Codex §43 (no irreducible runtime role found).
evidence_at_time: No current code with accountPurpose switch; BrokerageAccount stores no purpose/regime.
alternatives: runtime purpose switch (accountPurpose == income → X) explicitly forbidden (5576-5580)
rationale: Divergent Recommendations must be explained entirely by explicit machinery.
expected_consequences: PTS/Sawdust contrast becomes a falsification test for hidden label behavior.

title: UNRESOLVED / judgment-required is a distinct result class from affirmative inactivity (HOLD/WAIT/LET RESOLVE); REVIEW is attention/status, not an Alternative
context: §36 table included REVIEW as a Recommendation cell; §37 tightened it.
evidence_at_time: Existing RECONCILE-LIFECYCLE / DECISION-DEFERRED / NO-ACTION / HOLD states.
rationale: Do not disguise uncertainty as WAIT or manufacture a trade (5068-5070).
implementation: Doc 65 slice emits UNRESOLVED (ADR-019 impl note).
notes: Ratified portion is UNRESOLVED ≠ inactivity (ADR-019 item 9); REVIEW-as-attention clause is §37 working candidate only (proposal-only).

title: No new LVT Bet/Goal/Initiative, no new AR, no priority/horizon change for the governed-decision architecture promotion
context: §45 strategic/architecture-roadmap reconciliation after Principal decision A.
rationale: 'existing strategic direction is strengthened rather than changed' (7039); 'Architecture promotion must not silently become a priority/horizon decision.'
notes: 'The Principal did not change priority or horizon placement' is recorded as fact; the LVT mapping is reconciliation text; omitted from ADR-019.

title: AR dispositions: AR1 partially resolved (governed context/history only), AR6 materially resolved for first lifecycle-decision slice, AR7 narrowed, AR8 first-slice Decision replay substrate established; AR2–AR5, AR9/10 unchanged
expected_consequences: Broader portfolio/capital/lifecycle authority, Action/execution/outcome identity remain open.
notes: ADR-019 keeps AR1/6/7/8 summary; drops explicit AR2/3/4/5/9/10 'unchanged' statements.

title: Decomposition gate: regenerate/verify roadmap-projection.json (ADR-018 criterion) before implementation decomposition; afterwards do not reopen architecture absent concrete contradiction
Backend SQLite commit with backend-assigned recorded_at is sufficient temporal anchor under single-operator threat model; no cryptographic notarization
context: Muse proposed commitment/notary model; §42 rejected it for Wheelwright.
evidence_at_time: Single-operator deployment; no requirement to hide semantics from own backend.
alternatives: commitment/notary model with chain-head hashes and receipts (Muse §41)
rationale: Threat model excludes manual SQLite editing, filesystem rollback, mutually distrusting writers, regulatory non-repudiation (6301-6316).
expected_consequences: Stronger anchoring earned only if those threats become requirements.
subsequent: Codex §43 found no requirement forcing crypto anchoring.
notes: ADR-019 states the prohibition but not the explicit threat-model enumeration; ratification of the threat-model list itself is unclear.

title: Minimum decision/provenance contract (§37) and four→three-part slice (§38/§40) as bounded first-slice scope
context: Principal-authorized bounded semantic and architecture reconciliations following §§35–36.
rationale: Remaining semantic-model questions are not global blockers unless a specimen depends on them (5078).
subsequent: Partially superseded/absorbed into ADR-019 three record roles; §37's 14-item contract as a whole was not promoted.
amendments: §40 collapses Decision Trace + Disposition storage; §41 keeps them as distinct logical records.
notes: Status lines: 'working implementation-boundary candidate, not ratified' (4902); §38 'does not authorize implementation' (5095).

title: Muse used only with sanitized/generic problems; output is evidence not authority
rationale: 'This makes Muse especially useful where prior Wheelwright context could bias another actor toward confirming the existing model.' (5403)
notes: Wording is document summary of Principal guidance, not quoted Principal text.

title: Sawdust Growth/Compounding designation NOT ratified (experimental only)
context: Principal identified PTS (Income) vs Sawdust contrast.
expected_consequences: Requires explicit governance decision before operational use.
notes: Explicit non-decision; recorded to prevent cold actors treating Sawdust=Growth as ratified.
